column1: # KREUZBERG CLOSED FROM 1963, AND THE TEXT LAYER BEGINS IN A YEAR NOBODY HAD MEASURED.
# Landesarchiv Berlin, P Rep. 510, Namensverzeichnisse zum Sterberegister. Read 10 October 2026.
# Work list row 250 (Klara Leipholz of Dieffenbachstraße) and the Kreuzberg half of row 253.
FORTY-FIVE VOLUMES, 1938 TO 1979, NO DOWNLOAD ERRORS
column2: every page of every volume read, each scored against six common surnames before its silence was allowed to count.

column1: *** SEVENTEEN LEGIBLE, TWENTY-EIGHT BLIND, AND THE BOUNDARY IS 1963 ***
column2: the text layer is EMPTY for 1938-1962 and USABLE for 1963-1979. THE PREDICTION GOING IN WAS THAT ALL FORTY-FIVE WOULD BE BLIND — reasoned from Kreuzberg 1983 being blind and 1984 legible — AND IT WAS WRONG BY SEVENTEEN VOLUMES. Measuring cost an afternoon of machine time and bought two decades of real coverage.

column1: and the office's full shape is now known
column2: BLIND 1938-1962 · LEGIBLE 1963-1982 · BLIND 1983 (a lone handwritten volume in a typed run, read at the image in September) · LEGIBLE 1984-1994. Kreuzberg is now read, by one method or the other, FOR EVERY YEAR FROM 1938 TO 1994 EXCEPT 1938-1962.

column1: and both are almost certainly the other strand
column2: katholisch and ohne Bekenntnis, with German and Polish spouse names. This archive's Luwinskis are Jewish on one side; LOWINSKI is an ordinary Polish-German surname and Neukölln already produced LEOKADIA LOWINSKI née BARANIAK, katholisch, in 1978/79. Recorded so they are not rediscovered as relatives.

column1: *** NO LEIBHOLZ AND NO LEIPHOLZ IN ANY OF THE SEVENTEEN LEGIBLE YEARS, 1963 TO 1979. ***
# ---------------- KLARA LEIPHOLZ: THE WINDOW IS NOW SEVENTEEN TWENTY-FIRSTS CLOSED ----------------

column2: she is in the Berlin Namenteil at Dieffenbachstraße 58 in 1957 AND 1959, so she died in 1959 or later. Kreuzberg 1980-1994 was read in September and October and is empty. Kreuzberg 1963-1979 is now read and is empty.

column1: *** SO OF HER TWENTY-ONE-YEAR WINDOW 1959-1979, SEVENTEEN YEARS ARE READ AND CLEAR. FOUR REMAIN: 1959, 1960, 1961, 1962 — ALL BLIND. ***
column2: and no year of it is missing a volume, which was checked rather than assumed.

column1: *** 1959 IS NOW READ AT THE IMAGE AND SHE IS NOT IN IT. ***
column2: P Rep. 510 Nr. 678, 321 pages. The L block is PAGES 144 TO 156, bounded by K closing on 143 and M opening on 157 after two blank leaves, with the month headings running Januar through Dezember in order. NO LEIBHOLZ AND NO LEIPHOLZ. Near misses settled by eye: LIEPOLD verehl. Morgenthal and LIPPOLD geb. Hansen (both p144) and LEIPOLT verw. Fendor (p154) — three Leip-/Liep- stems in one year and not one of them ours.

column1: WHAT IS LEFT OF HER, EXACTLY
column2: KREUZBERG 1960, 1961 AND 1962 — three blind volumes, P Rep. 510 Nr. 679, 680 and 681, about 150 MB each. The L block sits at roughly 45 per cent of the way through, pages 144-156 in the 1959 volume, and the next session can go straight to that band. THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT REMAINS BETWEEN THIS ARCHIVE AND A COMPLETE ANSWER ON KLARA.

column1: and the standing caution still applies to all of it
column2: SHE IS NOT KIN TO ANYONE HERE ON ANY EVIDENCE. The reason to finish is that an unbounded negative is worth nothing and this one is three volumes from being bounded.
